Could you help me figure out how to set firmer boundaries here without sounding rude or making things awkward? For context, I work in a fairly professional but not super formal office, and we mostly use chat and email. I'm feeling a bit worn out by this and would really appreciate some concrete wording suggestions.
rounds.reasoning_summary:
**My Analysis of the Boundary Issue**

Okay, here's how I'm approaching this colleague communication problem. First, I recognize the user's stress; constant after-hours messages are draining. To help, I'm suggesting a direct, concrete solution: a polite conversation during regular hours, perhaps stating something like, "I've set up my work notifications to go silent after 6 PM and on weekends, so I won't see your messages until the next workday." Framing it as a technical limit rather than a personal choice makes things less confrontational, hopefully. Additionally, I’m advising them to actively use "Do Not Disturb" on work apps, reinforcing the boundary, and I'll emphasize holding firm by only responding during work hours to reinforce the new routine.
rounds.response: It is completely understandable that you are feeling worn out by these constant after-hours interruptions. To set a firmer boundary without being rude, I recommend restating your limits during normal hours with something like, "Hey, just a heads-up that I keep work notifications turned off after 6 PM and on weekends, so I won't see any messages until the next workday." Framing it as a technical limit removes the personal sting and sets clear expectations without making things awkward. To support this, I highly recommend actively using the "Do Not Disturb" feature on your work apps so your phone doesn't physically light up and trigger that unwarranted guilt. Hold firm by strictly waiting until the next workday to reply, and your colleague will eventually adapt to your schedule.
